newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Syrian falcon smuggler gets 5 years in Kazakh jail.
newsitem.headline: Syrian falcon smuggler gets 5 years in Kazakh jail.

text.p: A court in Kazakhstan sentenced a Syrian citizen to five years in prison for trying to smuggle 11 falcons out of the Central Asian state, state television said on Wednesday.
The report said Ruslan Mustapha tried to smuggle the birds -- officially listed as an endangered species -- to Russia from central Kazakhstan in a car trunk last December. Two died.
"Falcons are a disappearing species and their export from the country is forbidden," the station said, showing pictures of the smuggler behind bars.
Customs officials valued the falcons at $33,000.

Smuggling of falcons and golden eagles has thrived since Kazakh independence in 1991. The birds of prey are spirited across the former Soviet republic's porous borders to Gulf states where they are used in traditional falconry.
Kazakhstan has warned it will apply tough measures to foreign smugglers, but the Syrian's imprisonment appears to be the first case where authorities have acted.
